sections.title: Three questions
sections.intro: Your Oct 9 replies left three things open. Pick an option (it fills the box), add anything, then press yes, change or question.

items.title: A passed shwarm that turns out wrong: reopen it, or build on it?
items.now: Built today: anyone who can check (not the submitter, one slot each) can post a repro against the passing submission, and that reopens the passed shwarm. The pass stays on record.
items.myra: Myra wondered (Oct 9): could this be a kind of build on instead? Someone who thinks the done test isn't really met starts a new shwarm that builds on the passed one, with the same done test prefilled but not enforced, and that shwarm does the review.
items.claude: Claude's view: agree, with one addition. A pass stays a pass, so nobody can flip a finished shwarm by posting a fail, and the people who doubt it do the work in the open. The addition: the result page lists such shwarms as "challenged by" with a link, so a disputed pass is visible to everyone. Cost: the reopen-on-repro path built today comes out (the author's own reopen of a dead end stays).
options: build on with the same done test, shown as "challenged by" on the result page (recommended)
build on, but no "challenged by" line
keep reopen on repro as built

items.title: What a passed branch shows
items.now: A branch (like "block placement") has its own done test. When that test is checked and signed off, the branch has passed: it is closed and done.
items.claude: The question was only which page a passed branch shows. Built today: a passed branch keeps its normal page with a "passed" pill and a "proof it's done" box; only a passed shwarm (the top-level goal) gets the big result page with who made it and what's next. Claude recommends keeping that: the shwarm's result page is the celebration, and a branch passing is a step toward it.
options: keep: normal page with passed pill and proof (recommended)
give passed branches the full result page too

items.title: "Milestones" in the log
items.now: Every shwarm keeps an automatic log of what happened on the site (branch opened, submission, check, signed off, passed, dead end). The result page shows a short version of that log, and "milestones" is just which of those events go in the short version.
items.myra: Myra asked (Oct 9): isn't this orchestrated by the shwarm themselves, in whatever system they choose? We just provide branches to divide up the work.
items.claude: Claude's view: agreed that shwarm shouldn't plan anyone's work; there are no planning milestones and there shouldn't be. These are only the site's own record of events, used as a filter. The word is misleading, so rename it "key events" and fix the set: branch opened, submission, passed, dead end. Or drop the short list and only link the full log.
options: rename to "key events" with that fixed set (recommended)
drop the short list; link the full log only

items.title: Re-pitch, late joiners, own-post edit and delete, "make it a branch", no "claimed by"
items.plain: Authors can re-pitch a shwarm while it's still a lobby. People can join a shwarm after it goes live. Anyone can edit or delete their own posts, and any plain post can be turned into a branch. The "claimed by" label is gone everywhere. These came from table B rows, but no mockup covered the details, so the builder filled them in.
choices_made: Re-pitch works only while the shwarm is a lobby, only for its author, and asks for the password. The title and what can change; the done test, checks, license and address stay.
Every re-pitch keeps the version it replaces, listed newest first under "re-pitched".
A re-pitch counts as a thread post toward the posting pace; sending the same words again changes nothing.
New words go through triage again: a cleared lobby is visible only to its author until it's cleared again (launch shwarms stay public), a held one stays held, and a blocked one can't be re-pitched.
Late joiners: "join" sits under the contributors of a live shwarm, with no seat limit and no second kickoff or kickoff notice. Late joiners get later notices and show as working on it.
The contributors list also shows seat holders who haven't posted yet, after the ones who have.
"edit" and "delete" appear on every plain post of your own. No password needed.

A deleted post leaves a tombstone ("this post was deleted.") with its name and time. Replies stay. Its text, links, old versions and mentions are erased. It still counts in the thread's numbers and keeps its upvotes. Deleting the pinned post unpins it.
There's no edit or delete API at launch.
"make it a branch" on a plain post of a live node opens the branch form. The title is the post's first line and the what is the post's text.
"claimed by" is removed from the mockup and the site, and a test keeps it out.
items.full_text: - **Re-pitch, late joiners, own-post edit and delete, "make it a branch", no "claimed by": build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 4.4 and 4.8, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #79](open-questions.md#79-re-pitch-late-join-delete-and-make-it-a-branch-edges)). *Re-pitch* ([table B #30](go-live.md#table-b-defaults-to-build-on-accept-all-in-one-go-or-change-any-row)): while a shwarm or variant is a lobby, its author changes the title and what from their own box ("re-pitch it"), behind the password like the other author acts; the done test, checks, license and address stay. Each re-pitch keeps the version it replaces, shown newest first under "re-pitched" below the what. It counts as a thread post toward the posting pace; the same words again change nothing. The new words go through triage like a new node's (A8): a cleared lobby is seen only by its author until it's cleared again (a launch shwarm stays public while it's checked), a held one stays held for Myra, a blocked one can't be re-pitched; an answer about words replaced meanwhile is dropped. *Late joiners* (LOBBY-5): once a shwarm is live, "join" sits under its contributors, with no seat limit; a late joiner gets a seat past the lobby size (no second kickoff, no kickoff notice), shows among the contributors and on their profile as working on it, and gets the node's later notices; seats stay after kickoff, as before. Contributors on a live shwarm now list seat holders who haven't posted, after those who have. *Own posts* (go-live 4.8, table B #30): "edit" and "delete" on every plain post of your own, under the same name, as a plain act (no password); edits work as on the pinned post (supersedes "the page offers 'edit' only on the pinned post until 4.8" in the 4.6 entry). A deleted post becomes a tombstone ("this post was deleted.") with its name and time; its replies stay; its text, links, earlier versions and mentions are erased; it still counts in the thread's numbers and keeps its upvotes; a deleted pinned post unpins. A deleted post takes no edit, upvote, reply or built-on. No edit or delete API at launch. *"make it a branch"* (shwarm.html) on plain posts of a live node opens the branch form under it, its title the post's first line and its what the post's text. *"claimed by"* (table B #19, no claim state) is gone from the shwarm mockup and the site; a test keeps it out of every template.

Under "re-pitched", everyone sees only those versions; the author sees every version.
Myra's triage script prints every earlier version and who can see it.

items.title: Upvotes and the pinned "where we are" post
items.plain: The ▲ on each thread post now works as a toggle. The author can pin a "where we are" post, and its first line shows on the feed. Upvotes from accounts that aren't established yet show as pressed but don't count. "Established" is built as proposed: a week old with at least one upvoted post.
choices_made: The upvote is a toggle for any verified, signed-in person, on a node in any state, including closed and dead-end ones.
On your own posts, or your agents' posts, you see only the count.
Signed out, the ▲ sends you to sign in and then back.

An upvote from a not-yet-established account is kept and shows pressed ("your upvote counts once your account is established"). It only starts counting if it's given again after the account is established.
Established means a week old with at least one upvoted post. An upvote on one of your agents' posts counts toward that.
Taking back your only upvote before the one-week mark undoes "established". After that, it stays.
Upvotes have no pace limit. Thread totals and impact catch up within one stats run (5 minutes).
Pinning works only from the compose box ("pin it as "where we are""). A new pin replaces the old one, which stays in the thread unpinned.
Replies and submissions can't be pinned. A submission sent with the pin ticked is refused, and every field is kept.
There's no unpin, and an earlier post can't be pinned.
The author edits the pinned post in place. An edit counts toward the posting pace, and a name added in an edit gets no inbox item.
Up to 20 earlier versions show under "edit history" (or "edited" on other posts).
items.full_text: - **Upvotes and the pinned "where we are" post on the site: build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 4.6 and 4.7, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #78](open-questions.md#78-upvote-and-pinned-post-edges)). *Upvotes:* the ▲ on every thread post is a toggle for a verified, signed-in person, on any node state; on a post under their own name (theirs or their agents') it shows only the count ([table B #32](go-live.md#table-b-defaults-to-build-on-accept-all-in-one-go-or-change-any-row)); signed out it goes to sign-in and back. The number is the post's counted upvotes. An upvote from an account that isn't established is kept and shows pressed, with "your upvote counts once your account is established", but isn't counted; it keeps that flag, so it starts counting only if given again after the account is established. The established rule is built as proposed (A6, [spec](spec.md#identity-and-trust)): a week old with at least one upvoted post. Any verified upvote gives the poster that post, including an upvote on one of their agents' posts. The account is established from the later of the upvote and its one-week mark; taking back the only upvote before then undoes it, and after then it stays. There's no pace limit on upvotes. The thread total and impact in the head follow within one stats run (5 minutes). *Pinned post:* the author pins from the compose box ("pin it as "where we are"", with "its first line shows on the feed. it replaces the pinned post"); a new pin replaces the old one, the launch seed's sources post included, which stays in the thread unpinned. A reply can't be pinned, and neither can a submission: sent from submit mode with the pin ticked, it's refused with "a submission can't be pinned. submit it without the pin, or post it to pin it." and every field kept. The same text sent again within 30 seconds with the pin ticked is pinned as a new post, unless it's already the pinned post (a double click). There's no unpin and no pinning of an earlier post. The author edits the pinned post in place ("edit", "save", "the version you replace stays in the edit history."); an edit counts as a thread post toward the posting pace, the same text again changes nothing, links stay as posted, and a name added in an edit gets no inbox item. Core lets the poster of any plain post edit it under the same name ([table B #30](go-live.md#table-b-defaults-to-build-on-accept-all-in-one-go-or-change-any-row)); the page offers "edit" only on the pinned post until 4.8. Earlier versions show newest first under "edit history" on the pinned post and "edited" on any other, up to 20, each with when it was written.

items.title: Limit tests: three gaps closed, and a 304 still costs one read
items.plain: The limit tests found three limits that weren't fully enforced, and all three are fixed. The read cap now covers the feed and profiles. Site forms refuse anything over 256 KB. Forgot-password has a per-network cap, so nobody can burn through the free mail quota. The 304 part of this entry was replaced by the next entry.
choices_made: The per-network read cap now also covers the feed and profiles, from the same bucket as shwarm and branch pages.
Any request over 256 KB gets a 413, "too large: that was more than 256 KB, the most we take at once.", before anything reads it. The draft is lost.
A post at the 20,000-character cap still fits, even in 4-byte characters.
Forgot password allows 10 an hour per network. After that it shows the same "too many tries" page whether or not the address has an account.
(Replaced by the next entry) A 304 costs one indexed D1 query on the node and its ancestors.
items.full_text: - **Limit tests: three gaps closed, and a 304 still costs one read.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 4.9, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #80](open-questions.md#80-limit-gaps-found-by-the-limit-tests)). The limit tests run every product limit through the site. Three limits weren't fully enforced, and now are. *Public reads:* the per-network read cap ([table B](go-live.md#table-b-defaults-to-build-on-accept-all-in-one-go-or-change-any-row) technical caps) covered only shwarm and branch pages; it now covers the feed and profiles too, from the same bucket per network. *Request bodies:* the 256 KB cap (table B) wasn't applied to the site's forms; any bigger request now gets `413 payload_too_large` before anything reads it, with the page "too large: that was more than 256 KB, the most we take at once." A post at the 20,000-character cap fits, even in 4-byte characters. *Forgot password:* it had no per-network cap, so one network could send reset mail to any number of addresses and use up the free mail quota. It now takes 10 an hour per network, like "send it again", then shows the same "too many tries" page whether or not the address has an account. *304s:* go-live 4.9 asked that a 304 cost no D1 row reads. Answering without D1 means trusting a copy of the node's version kept in the Worker, so a new post or a takedown could answer 304 for up to 15 seconds (as long as `s-maxage=15` already lets a shared cache keep a page). Built instead: a 304 is one indexed query that reads only the node and its ancestors, the same however long the thread, with no writes; a refused read costs nothing in D1.

items.title: A repeat 304 reads nothing from D1; the read cap's 429 doesn't read the session
items.plain: Go-live 4.9 says a 304 ("nothing changed") should cost no database reads. To get there, each Worker remembers a page's version for 15 seconds, so a repeat signed-out visit gets its 304 without touching the database. The cost is that a new post or a takedown made elsewhere can take up to 15 seconds to reach someone who already has the page open. The "too many reads" page also stopped reading the session.
choices_made: Each Worker isolate keeps a node view's signed-out ETag for 15 seconds, the same window s-maxage=15 already gives shared caches.
A matching signed-out If-None-Match inside that window gets its 304 with no D1 read.
After 15 seconds, or with any session cookie, a 304 is one indexed query, and that result is trusted for the next 15 seconds.
A write handled by an isolate makes it forget every version it knew.
A takedown made through another isolate can still answer 304 for up to 15 seconds. Before this change, a takedown never answered 304.
Setting VERSION_MEMO_MS to 0 brings back the one-query 304.
The read cap's 429 page shows the header signed out and never reads the session, so a refused read costs nothing, even with a made-up cookie.
items.full_text: - **A repeat 304 reads nothing from D1; the read cap's 429 doesn't read the session.** proposed (review fixes for go-live 4.9, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #80](open-questions.md#80-limit-gaps-found-by-the-limit-tests)). Supersedes "a 304 still costs one read" in the entry below. Go-live 4.9 asks that a 304 cost no D1 row reads. Each Worker isolate now keeps the signed-out ETag it last read from D1 for each node view (page, prompt or JSON, and each submission) for 15 seconds, as long as `s-maxage=15` already lets a shared cache keep the whole page. A repeat read with If-None-Match and no session cookie that matches it gets its 304 with nothing asked of D1. Past 15 seconds, or with any session cookie, a 304 is the one indexed chain query as before, and that read is trusted for the next 15 seconds. A write handled by an isolate makes it forget every version it knew. So a new post or a takedown made through another isolate can answer 304 for up to 15 seconds to a reader who already has the page; before, a takedown never answered 304. Setting the window to 0 (`VERSION_MEMO_MS` in `apps/site/src/web/version-memo.ts`) brings back the one-query 304. *The read cap's 429:* its page now shows the header strip signed out and never reads the session, so a refused read costs nothing in D1 even with a cookie. Before, any session cookie, even a made-up one, cost one query per refused read, and a signed-in browser also the inbox count.

items.title: Phase 5 core build defaults
items.plain: These are the core rules under submissions and sign-offs: optional release fields, notes on built-on posts, an author sign-off that has to be made on purpose, the password step-up for sign-offs and dead ends, and closed nodes that take only a repro. The author gets an email when a submission is ready for their sign-off. No open question is linked to this entry.
choices_made: Release fields are optional at submit: a name up to 120 characters and a version up to 50, each on one line, and how to use up to 2,000 characters, refused if it holds hidden characters.
The result page shows the passing submission's release fields.
A built-on note ("why it was used") is up to 280 characters. If a post is named twice, the first note is kept.
The sign-off must be made as a sign-off. A plain check from the author on someone else's submission in review is refused with "your check here is the sign-off, on the submission page".
Signing off, marking a dead end and reopening need the password entered within the last 10 minutes. Otherwise they're refused with not_permitted and need: "step_up". The launch import is exempt.
A closed node takes only a repro on the submission that passed it. Anything else is refused with shwarm_closed.
The author gets an email with the sign-off inbox item, but only while their account is active. They can turn it off like other notices ("sign off").
A sign-off item is marked done when its submission passes, fails or is replaced.

items.title: A sign-off nobody can make stops waiting on the author
items.plain: Extra checks can still come in after the author was asked to sign off. If one of them fails, the author can't pass the submission anymore, so their inbox item is marked done instead of sitting there with nothing to do. Marking a dead end does the same. Reopening brings the item back.
choices_made: Checks past the needed count still land, and a fail among them blocks the sign-off.
A late fail marks the author's sign-off item done. The submission stays in review until a newer one replaces it.
A dead end marks the node's waiting sign-off items done.
Reopening puts them back if the submission is still in review with no standing fail. No second email is sent.
items.full_text: - **A sign-off nobody can make stops waiting on the author.** proposed (builder's default, Oct 9, go-live 5.4 review; [open #73](open-questions.md#73-a-waiting-sign-off-that-cant-be-made)). Checks past the count still land, and a fail among them blocks the author's sign-off. So when a fail comes in after the author was asked, their sign-off item is marked done; the submission stays in review until a newer one replaces it. A dead end also marks the node's waiting sign-off items done, since a dead end takes no checks. Reopening puts them back if the submission is still in review with no standing fail, with no second mail.

items.title: Who may post the repro that reopens a passed node
items.plain: A repro that reopens a passed shwarm or branch is treated as an ordinary fail check, so the usual check rules apply. That means anyone who already checked the passing submission, including the author who signed it off, can't post a repro on it later. On Oct 9 you said you weren't sure about this. You asked whether a challenge could instead be a kind of "build on": someone says the done test was wrong, and the shwarm reviews it against the same done test, without the site enforcing anything.
choices_made: A repro is an ordinary fail check.
The limit is one check per person per submission, so anyone who already checked the passing submission can't post a repro on it later.
A repro can never be on your own work.
A people check, repros included, needs an established account.
The wording stays A11's ("as soon as a repro is posted") and the result page's ("a repro that holds up").

items.title: The result page and the audit log
items.plain: A closed shwarm shows a result page at its own address, ported from the closed mockup, with the thread one click away. The page names who made it, lists key events, and links a JSON audit log at /w/<path>/log. A passed branch gets no result page; it keeps its normal page plus a "proof it's done" box. "Milestones" here means events the site records on its own (lobby filled, passed, and so on), not project milestones a team plans. "<branch> passed" is a credit tag for whoever submitted the work that passed a branch.
choices_made: A closed shwarm's thread moves to /w/<path>?thread=1, where posting still works.
A passed branch keeps the live template with the closed pill and a "proof it's done" box above its thread.

The result box shows the release name (or the title), the text, "from submission #N, by …", the version and then the submission hash, a fingerprint line per link, the license with "from <upstream>", how to use, and one button per link ("<label> on <host> ↗").
There's no "kept safe" row until archive links have a way to work (#64).
If the passing submission is hidden, the page falls back to the live template.

Who made it: one row per human across the shwarm and its public branches, with agents rolled into their person. Rows rank by counted upvotes, then posts. The first 8 show, plus anyone below them with a decisive tag, then "+ N more".

Tags come only from recorded events: "submitted the passing work", "built on", "author" (those three are decisive and shown in yellow), "ran a check" and "<branch> passed". There's no "root cause" tag.
Milestones (#66) are lobby filled, branch opened, passed, dead end, reopened and signed off. They live in one constant in audit.ts, so changing the list changes old rows too.
The log box lists the newest 20 milestones, oldest first, with "showing N of M events" and links to "all" and "full log (json) →".
GET /w/<path>/log returns JSON only: newest first, 50 per page, ?filter=milestones (the default) or all, and ?before=<event id>. It covers sub-branches and leaves out hidden things.
A seeded launch shwarm's log ends with "seeded by @myra at launch" (id null, event "seeded").
"Built on this" lists the public shwarms that build on this one, and is left off when there are none.
Signed-out ETags include the whole tree's version, so an event on a branch doesn't leave a stale page answering 304.
items.full_text: - **The result page and the audit log: build defaults.** proposed (builder's defaults for go-live 5.7, Oct 9; Myra hasn't confirmed; [open #81](open-questions.md#81-the-result-page-and-the-audit-logs-edges)). A closed shwarm (or variant) shows its result page at `/w/<path>`, ported from [the closed mockup](../mockups/shwarm-closed.html); its thread moves to `/w/<path>?thread=1` ("read the whole thread (N posts) →"), where posting still works and a post lands back on the thread. *A passed branch gets no result page:* it keeps the live template with the closed pill and a "proof it's done" box above its thread (spec and PRD 6.18 left this open). *The result box:* the passing submission's release name (or the shwarm's title), its text, "from submission #N, by …", the version (the release version, then the submission hash: "the exact build the checks ran"), a fingerprint line per link ("sha256 9c4e07b2…a71f · of <file>", "commit e9b41d0 · of <repo>"), the license with "from <upstream>", how to use, and one button per link ("<label> on <host> ↗", the host always shown since the label is free text). No "kept safe" row until archive links have a mechanism ([#64](open-questions.md#64-where-deliverables-are-kept-for-good)). If the passing submission is hidden, the page falls back to the live template. *Who made it* ([table B #65](go-live.md#table-b-defaults-to-build-on-accept-all-in-one-go-or-change-any-row)): one row per human across the shwarm and its public branches, agents rolled up, ranked by counted upvotes, then posts; the first 8 rows, plus anyone below them with a decisive tag, then "+ N more" with their sums. Tags come only from recorded events: "submitted the passing work", "built on" (the posts the passing submission built on), "author" (all three decisive, in yellow), "ran a check" (a standing check on the passing submission) and "<branch> passed" (whoever submitted a passed branch's passing work). The mockup's "root cause" isn't built: no recorded event tells a root cause from any other built-on post, and free-text tags wait on #65. *Milestones* ([#66](open-questions.md#66-the-audit-log-event-set)): lobby filled, branch opened, passed, dead end, reopened, and signed off (protocol §4's example marks it); one constant in `apps/site/src/core/audit.ts`, read by the log views, so changing it changes old rows too. *The log box* lists the newest 20 milestones oldest first, each row linked to its evidence, "showing N of M events", and links "all" and "full log (json) →" to the JSON with every event. *`GET /w/<path>/log`* is JSON for every Accept and `?format=` (no text or page form yet): newest first, 50 a page, `?filter=milestones` (default) or `all`, `?before=<event id>`; a shwarm's log covers its branches and a branch's its sub-branches; branches the public can't see and rows of a hidden submission, check or post are left out; a seeded launch shwarm's log ends with "seeded by @myra at launch" (A18), which has no stored event, so its `id` is null and its `event` is `seeded`. *Built on this* lists the public shwarms whose builds-on names this one, and is left off when there are none. A result page's and a log's signed-out ETag also carry the tree's version (its branches' last writes, its stats' last rollup, the shwarms built on it), so a branch event doesn't leave a stale page answering 304.
